title: Identities & trig equations
examples: How do I start when I see sin squared plus cos squared?
What is the easiest way to solve for x when I have tan x?
If I solve for x, do I need to worry about the period?

explain.say: Today we look at some useful identities in trigonometry. We will learn three key rules. These rules help us simplify complex trig expressions. Let us start with the first fundamental identity.

items: Start with the first fundamental identity
Solve equations over a specific interval

explain.say: The first identity is sin squared x plus cos squared x equals one. This is true for every angle x. Think of it like a special relationship always holding true. For example, if x is zero degrees, sin zero is zero and cos zero is one. So zero squared plus one squared equals one. This works perfectly.

Next, we remember the definition of the tangent function. Tangent of x is sin of x divided by cos of x. This is a crucial ratio in trigonometry. For example, if we use an angle where sin is three and cos is four, then tan x is three divided by four. This keeps our expressions neat.

draw.text: tan x = sin x / cos x

explain.say: Finally, we learn to solve trig equations over a specific interval. We must always check the given range for x. For example, if we solve for sin x equals one divided by two in the interval zero to two pi. The solutions are pi divided by six and five pi divided by six. Remember to respect the boundaries.

items: Check the given range for x

faq.q: Why do I have to use the identity sin squared x plus cos squared x equals one?
faq.a: This identity is fundamental because it allows you to rewrite expressions that look complicated. It lets you reduce the number of different trig functions you see. You might also hear this as 'prove the identity' or 'what is the Pythagorean identity for sine and cosine?'
asks: What is the main trig identity?
How do I simplify using sin²x + cos²x = 1?

faq.q: When can I use tan x equals sin x divided by cos x?
faq.a: You can use this whenever you need to change an expression involving tangent into terms of sine and cosine. This helps you use the other identities we know. Another way to ask this is 'express tan in sin and cos' or 'what is tan x as a ratio?'
asks: How do I write tan using sin and cos?
Can I change tan to sin over cos?

faq.q: If I solve for x, do I always find all the answers?
faq.a: No, you must always check the given interval for x. The interval tells you exactly which values are valid solutions. If no interval is given, you must state the general solution form. You could also ask 'what is the domain for the solutions?'
asks: Do I need to worry about the range?
How do I write the general solution?

faq.q: What happens if cos x is zero when I use tan x?
faq.a: If cos x is zero, then tan x is undefined at that point. You must check the domain restrictions first. This means the angle x cannot be ninety degrees or two hundred seventy degrees in radians. You might also ask 'where is tan undefined?'
asks: Is there an exception for tan x?
What if the denominator is zero?

faq.q: Can I use the identity on any angle?
faq.a: Yes, the identity sin squared x plus cos squared x equals one is true for all real numbers x. It is a universal truth in trigonometry. You might also ask 'is this identity always true?'
asks: Does this identity work for all angles?

facts: The identity sin squared x plus cos squared x equals one is always true.
The tangent function is defined as the ratio of sine to cosine. This is tan x equals sin x divided by cos x.
When solving trig equations, always check the specified interval for x.
The tangent function is undefined when the cosine value is zero.

quiz.say: If sin x equals one half and cos x equals the square root of three divided by two, what is the value of sin²x plus cos²x?
quiz.why: The identity sin squared x plus cos squared x equals one is always true, so the answer must be one.

wrong.1: This is a common mistake because you might only use the sine value given.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you incorrectly add the squares of the given values.
wrong.3: This might happen if you forget to square one of the initial values.

quiz.say: What is the value of tan x if sin x equals three and cos x equals four?
quiz.show: tan x = sin x / cos x
quiz.why: By definition, tangent is sine divided by cosine, so three divided by four is correct.

wrong.1: This mistake occurs if you incorrectly add the values of sin x and cos x.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you multiply the two given values instead of dividing.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because you must perform division, not just approximate the ratio.

quiz.say: Find all solutions for sin x equals zero in the interval zero to two pi.
quiz.why: Sine is zero at the angles zero and pi within the specified range of zero to two pi.

wrong.0: Two pi is the same angle as zero in a full circle, but the interval usually includes zero and excludes two pi for unique solutions.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the interval starts at zero, so zero must be included if it is a solution.
wrong.2: This mistake forgets that sine is also zero at the pi angle within the given range.
